title: Effusion
identity: Brendan Faegre, Effusion (2013/14), c. 11 minutes. The inspected Donemus D15383 preview is a transposed score for soprano saxophone and piano. The program note describes a flute/piano timbral starting concept, but the inspected score itself is the soprano-saxophone version.

evidence.claim: Composer site lists the soprano-saxophone-and-piano alternative, duration 11 minutes, and links program note, video, and score/parts.
Donemus catalog identifies the purchasable work and its performance note, including flutter tongue, slap tongue, blown air, and prepared/altered piano color.
Donemus preview title and copyright pages identify the 2013/14 soprano saxophone and piano version as a transposed score, duration c. 11 minutes, D15383.

The preview’s performance notes describe relative saxophone/piano dynamics and prepared piano timbres coordinated with slap-tongue, flutter-tongue, and blown-air sounds; footnotes explain techniques where they occur.
Composer’s program note says the piece began from a flute/piano timbral concept, while the public score is explicitly the soprano-saxophone version.
evidence.source_name: Donemus public preview, program note and score

score_observations.claim: Opening page is marked quarter=96, “Rhythmically precise, grooving”; the soprano saxophone begins with rests and short detached/slap-tongue gestures over a prepared-piano ostinato. The opening moves through changing meters, including 5/4 and 4/4.
score_observations.source_name: Donemus public score preview, opening page

score_observations.claim: The later inspected page includes 3/8, 2/4, and 5/4 changes; saxophone uses blown air, half slap, flutter-tongue, held tones and short rests, with abrupt p-to-ff swells. Piano footnotes call for brushing the lowest strings to imitate saxophone air sound.
score_observations.source_name: Donemus public score preview, PDF p. 5 / printed p. 3

review_focus: Inference from inspected pages: assess rhythmic precision through irregular meter, timing and control of slap-tongue, air and flutter-tongue colors, large dynamic shifts, and balance with the prepared piano. Full written range remains unknown.
collection_flag: Composer lists flute/piano and soprano saxophone/piano scorings; the inspected score is explicitly the transposed soprano version. The composer’s timbral program note refers to the originating flute concept, while notation verifies dedicated soprano-saxophone writing in this edition.
